text:
emma_ae: Heads-up — Optima trial load test started returning 5xxs during ramp. They're sending ~120-160 rps bursts. Live demo in 18m, need a quick mitigation we can apply without breaking anything.

lee_support: Any region/model and an example error/req id?

emma_ae: Region: us-east-1, model: redwood-open-3b-q4-hosted. Example from their harness: 
```
POST /v1/generate
HTTP/1.1 502 Bad Gateway
x-rw-queue-depth: 59
{"error":"upstream overloaded","request_id":"req_opt_9001"}
```
Also seeing 504s.

sam_infra: Classic queue saturation + autoscaler lag. Fast options (in order of speed/risk):
- API-key scoped soft-failover to the 1B variant (no infra spin)
- temporarily enable per-customer burstpool attach (if AE ok)
- set pool min_replicas=1 for the 3B pool (warmer but costs more)

jordan_se: We should prefer failover for a demo. Can route only high-latency requests to the smaller model so most calls keep 3B.

sam_infra: Commands I can run now: 
```
# API-key soft failover (zero infra spin)
redwoodctl api-keys update --id key-optima --set failover_model=redwood-open-1b-q4 --set failover_latency_threshold=600ms
# allow burstpool attach (if customer agrees)
redwoodctl customers update --id optima --set allow_burst=true
# quick warm replica (if needed)
redwoodctl pool update redwood-open-3b-q4 --region us-east-1 --min-replicas 1
```

lee_support: If AE asks about cost for the warm replica, what should I tell them?

sam_infra: Quick back-of-envelope for us-east: min_replicas=1 for 3B ~+$700/day, so for a 1-hour demo it's ~+$30. Soft-failover is essentially zero incremental infra cost for short spikes.

emma_ae: AE asked whether enabling allow_burst affects data residency or logs. They want reassurance before approving.

jordan_se: Short answer: routing/burst settings don't change region residency; logs for hosted us-east customers remain in the us-east retention bucket. If they need a signed addendum escalate to Legal.

inc-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-3200-01 — "optima trial: upstream overload" (link: https://internal.incidents/INC-2026-3200-01)

sam_infra: I'll flip the API-key failover now (low-risk). Emma, please enable burstpool only if AE consents. Also grab the proxy log bundle for req_opt_9001: `curl -H \"x-request-id: req_opt_9001\" https://logs.internal/bundle` and run `redwoodctl metrics query --name queue_depth --since 20m --filter customer=optima`.

emma_ae: Flipped failover to 1B at 600ms and asked the AE about burst. Logs/metrics uploaded to the incident.

lee_support: After the failover flip, 502/504 errors dropped to single digits within 90s and latency stabilized. Demo team notified and proceeding.

sam_infra: Follow-ups to track in the incident:
- audit trial routing defaults (why burstpool didn't auto-attach at queue_depth>50)
- consider a prewarm API for scheduled demos to prebind 1 replica for X minutes
- add a short KB for AEs: "If demo >80rps expected, request prewarm or enable failover" with cost bullets

emma_ae: AE completed the demo successfully and appreciated the quick decision. Leaving the incident open for infra follow-ups. :white_check_mark:
